football_factors.reason: DAL's QB efficiency is significantly higher than CLE's this season (0.310 EPA/play difference) — a gap that shapes drive consistency and big-play rate.

football_factors.name: Turnover Edge
football_factors.reason: DAL wins the turnover battle modestly — a 0.79 turnover-per-game edge that creates shorter fields and extra possessions.

football_factors.name: Offensive Efficiency
football_factors.reason: DAL's offense generates significantly more expected points per play than CLE's (0.190 EPA/play difference), keeping drives alive and converting more consistently.

football_factors.name: Defensive Resistance
football_factors.reason: DAL's defense is slightly more stingy than CLE's — allowing 0.042 fewer EPA per play and limiting opponent scoring opportunities.

football_factors.reason: DAL wins the pass rush vs. protection battle slightly (0.008 sack-rate edge) — a mismatch that can collapse key third-down drives.

explanation: The model leans CLE (0-0), but DAL owns the QB Efficiency edge. The lean is built primarily on market signals — treat DAL's QB Efficiency advantage as the live upset path.

headline: Model lean: JAX at 61.5%
football_story: The model leans JAX (1-4), but CHI owns the Recent Form edge. JAX are 1-2 last 3. The lean is built primarily on market signals — treat CHI's Recent Form advantage as the live upset path.
primary_reason: JAX's pass-rush-vs-protection matchup gives them a 2.6% sack-rate edge. Pressure collapses routes, forces early throws, and creates negative plays.
secondary_reason: The primary football edge carries most of the weight — no clear secondary factor reinforces JAX.
risk_factor: CHI owns the Recent Form edge. CHI has been the hotter team over the last 3 games (composite form edge: 0.89). Trajectory matters — injuries, scheme changes, and momentum all show up here first.
flip_scenarios: If JAX loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.
If CHI's protection neutralizes early pressure, JAX's defensive edge shrinks.
If CHI converts its EPA edge into red-zone touchdowns, the model's lean can flip.

factor_cards.name: Recent Form
factor_cards.reason: CHI has been the hotter team over the last 3 games (composite form edge: 0.89). Trajectory matters — injuries, scheme changes, and momentum all show up here first.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Recent three-game form helps identify whether the matchup is being shaped by current trajectory.
factor_cards.football_translation: Recent form catches whether current performance is moving ahead of or behind season-long averages.

factor_cards.name: Turnover Control
factor_cards.reason: CHI wins the turnover battle by 1.06 turnovers/game on average. Each extra possession is worth roughly 2–3 expected points of field position.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: A possession swing can erase a statistical edge quickly, especially in close probability ranges.
factor_cards.football_translation: Turnovers swing possessions, field position, and hidden scoring chances.

factor_cards.name: EPA/play
factor_cards.reason: CHI creates meaningfully more expected value per play than JAX (0.123 EPA/play edge). Consistent EPA generation sustains drives without needing explosive plays.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Teams creating more EPA per snap can score without relying only on turnovers or short fields.
factor_cards.football_translation: EPA/play measures down-to-down value creation, not just yards or final score.

factor_cards.name: Sack Pressure
factor_cards.reason: JAX's pass-rush-vs-protection matchup gives them a 2.6% sack-rate edge. Pressure collapses routes, forces early throws, and creates negative plays.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Pressure can force checkdowns, stalled drives, negative plays, and turnover-worthy throws.
factor_cards.football_translation: Pressure changes timing, limits deep concepts, and can kill third-down drives.

factor_cards.name: Success Rate
factor_cards.reason: CHI converts 0.025 more plays 'on schedule' (first-down-gain rate). Staying on schedule limits predictable down-and-distance for the defense.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: A success-rate edge points to repeatable drive quality rather than one-off explosive plays.
factor_cards.football_translation: Success rate captures whether an offense stays ahead of the chains snap after snap.

factor_cards.name: QB Efficiency
factor_cards.reason: C.Williams holds a slightly QB efficiency edge over T.Lawrence (0.039 EPA/play advantage). Efficient passers sustain drives and create explosive plays without needing short fields.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Quarterback efficiency is usually the cleanest single football signal because it drives both explosive plays and third-down survival.
factor_cards.football_translation: Efficient quarterbacks sustain drives and create explosive plays without needing perfect field position.

headline: Clear edge: CHI at 66.9%
football_story: CHI (4-4) hold a meaningful edge in Recent Form and Success Rate. CHI enter at 1-2 last 3. The market agrees.

secondary_reason: CHI converts 0.016 more plays 'on schedule' (first-down-gain rate). Staying on schedule limits predictable down-and-distance for the defense.

game_diagnosis.headline: Clear edge: HOU at 72.6%
game_diagnosis.football_story: HOU (7-4) hold a meaningful edge in Recent Form and Turnover Control. HOU enter at 1-2 last 3. Divisional game — expect a tighter margin than the stats suggest. The market agrees.
game_diagnosis.primary_reason: HOU has been the hotter team over the last 3 games (composite form edge: 0.37). Trajectory matters — injuries, scheme changes, and momentum all show up here first.
game_diagnosis.secondary_reason: HOU wins the turnover battle by 0.39 turnovers/game on average. Each extra possession is worth roughly 2–3 expected points of field position.
game_diagnosis.risk_factor: TEN owns the Sack Pressure edge. TEN's pass-rush-vs-protection matchup gives them a 3.7% sack-rate edge. Pressure collapses routes, forces early throws, and creates negative plays.
flip_scenarios: If HOU loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.
If HOU cannot keep the quarterback clean, stalled drives become the main upset path.
If HOU's EPA/play falls below neutral on early downs, the matchup becomes script-dependent.

factor_cards.football_translation: Turnovers swing possessions, field position, and hidden scoring chances.

factor_cards.why_it_matters: A success-rate edge points to repeatable drive quality rather than one-off explosive plays.
factor_cards.football_translation: Success rate captures whether an offense stays ahead of the chains snap after snap.

headline: Model lean: IND at 60.9%
football_story: IND (6-8) hold a meaningful edge in Recent Form and Sack Pressure. IND enter at 1-2 last 3. Divisional game — expect a tighter margin than the stats suggest. The market agrees.
primary_reason: IND has been the hotter team over the last 3 games (composite form edge: 0.16). Trajectory matters — injuries, scheme changes, and momentum all show up here first.
secondary_reason: IND's pass-rush-vs-protection matchup gives them a 1.3% sack-rate edge. Pressure collapses routes, forces early throws, and creates negative plays.
risk_factor: TEN owns the QB Efficiency edge. W.Levis holds a slightly QB efficiency edge over A.Richardson (0.043 EPA/play advantage). Efficient passers sustain drives and create explosive plays without needing short fields.
flip_scenarios: If IND loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.
If TEN's protection neutralizes early pressure, IND's defensive edge shrinks.
If IND's EPA/play falls below neutral on early downs, the matchup becomes script-dependent.

market_context.interpretation: Market inputs help calibrate baseline team strength, but football diagnosis sections intentionally avoid citing Vegas as the cause.

factor_cards.name: Recent Form
factor_cards.reason: IND has been the hotter team over the last 3 games (composite form edge: 0.16). Trajectory matters — injuries, scheme changes, and momentum all show up here first.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Recent three-game form helps identify whether the matchup is being shaped by current trajectory.
factor_cards.football_translation: Recent form catches whether current performance is moving ahead of or behind season-long averages.

factor_cards.name: Sack Pressure
factor_cards.reason: IND's pass-rush-vs-protection matchup gives them a 1.3% sack-rate edge. Pressure collapses routes, forces early throws, and creates negative plays.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Pressure can force checkdowns, stalled drives, negative plays, and turnover-worthy throws.
factor_cards.football_translation: Pressure changes timing, limits deep concepts, and can kill third-down drives.

factor_cards.name: QB Efficiency
factor_cards.reason: W.Levis holds a slightly QB efficiency edge over A.Richardson (0.043 EPA/play advantage). Efficient passers sustain drives and create explosive plays without needing short fields.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Quarterback efficiency is usually the cleanest single football signal because it drives both explosive plays and third-down survival.
factor_cards.football_translation: Efficient quarterbacks sustain drives and create explosive plays without needing perfect field position.

factor_cards.name: Turnover Control
factor_cards.reason: TEN wins the turnover battle by 0.18 turnovers/game on average. Each extra possession is worth roughly 2–3 expected points of field position.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: A possession swing can erase a statistical edge quickly, especially in close probability ranges.
factor_cards.football_translation: Turnovers swing possessions, field position, and hidden scoring chances.

factor_cards.name: EPA/play
factor_cards.reason: IND creates slightly more expected value per play than TEN (0.022 EPA/play edge). Consistent EPA generation sustains drives without needing explosive plays.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: Teams creating more EPA per snap can score without relying only on turnovers or short fields.
factor_cards.football_translation: EPA/play measures down-to-down value creation, not just yards or final score.

factor_cards.name: Success Rate
factor_cards.reason: IND converts 0.002 more plays 'on schedule' (first-down-gain rate). Staying on schedule limits predictable down-and-distance for the defense.
factor_cards.why_it_matters: A success-rate edge points to repeatable drive quality rather than one-off explosive plays.
factor_cards.football_translation: Success rate captures whether an offense stays ahead of the chains snap after snap.

factor_cards.why_it_matters: A possession swing can erase a statistical edge quickly, especially in close probability ranges.
factor_cards.football_translation: Turnovers swing possessions, field position, and hidden scoring chances.

factor_cards.football_translation: Recent form catches whether current performance is moving ahead of or behind season-long averages.
